subject: landslide into reservoir
title: What If a Mountain Fell Into a Reservoir? In 1963 the Dam Held, the Wave Didn't

scenes.text: What if a mountainside slid into a full reservoir? In 1963, the dam survived. The wave didn't care.
The Vajont dam in the Italian Alps was the world's tallest when it was built. Behind it, a flank of Monte Toc had been creeping for years.
October 9, 1963, 10:39 at night. About 270 million cubic metres of rock let go at once, a slab 250 metres thick, moving at up to 90 kilometres an hour.
It hit the water. The reservoir leapt 250 metres above the dam crest and poured over the top.
A wave about 70 metres high ran down the gorge into Longarone and four villages. About 2,000 people died in minutes.
The dam took eight times the force it was designed for and stood. It still stands today, holding back nothing.

description:
What if an entire mountainside slid into a reservoir? On 9 October 1963, about 270 million cubic metres of Monte Toc collapsed into the lake behind Italy's Vajont dam, then the tallest dam in the world, at speeds up to about 90 kilometres an hour.
The displaced water rose some 250 metres above the dam and a wave around 70 metres high destroyed Longarone and nearby villages, killing about 2,000 people. The dam itself withstood roughly eight times its design load and still stands, empty.
What should we run through next?
